claims.text: Extended warranty companies look for technical reasons to deny otherwise legitimate claims
Modifying a vehicle covered by an extended warranty can be used to void or deny coverage
Extended warranty claim inspections and reconsiderations can take days, leaving a vehicle unusable during the wait
Extended warranty providers commonly request service records before approving a claim, which can delay repairs
Extended warranties (vehicle service contracts) are different products from the factory warranty that comes with a new car

Buying an extended warranty while the manufacturer's factory warranty is still active is unnecessary overlap

A warranty company that denies more claims keeps more of the money it collected in premiums, creating an incentive to deny

Vehicle service contracts can include arbitration clauses that require customers to resolve disputes outside of court
Extended warranties are more worthwhile for complex products with more electronics or expensive components that are more prone to costly failures

Extended warranty pricing varies by brand reliability -- less reliable brands cost more to insure

Buyers who plan to keep a car long after the factory warranty ends benefit most from an extended warranty

Victims of auto warranty telemarketing scams often find the coverage sold is far less than what the phone pitch described
Buying an extended warranty whose term exceeds how long you plan to keep or how far you'll drive the car wastes money on unused coverage
Dealerships often profit more from financing, service and add-on products like extended warranties than from the vehicle sale itself

Online checkout flows are deliberately designed to increase how often shoppers opt into an extended warranty or protection plan

Mechanics refuse to work with certain extended warranty companies because disputing and collecting payment from them is difficult.

Extended warranty plans typically exclude pre-existing conditions and problems that existed before the contract began.

A money-back guarantee lets a buyer return an extended warranty within a short window for a refund.
Extended warranty claims often fail because there are not enough skilled technicians available to do the repair work.
When warranty companies subcontract repairs to the cheapest provider, the work may not be done by a properly qualified technician.
Manufacturers often prioritize shipping new products over supplying parts for warranty repairs, lengthening repair wait times.
An extended warranty sold by a retailer without its own repair department is passed to a third party, increasing the risk of delays and denials.
An extended warranty is more likely to be worth it when the seller does its own repairs with its own technicians and equipment.
Some extended warranty providers refund part of the cost as a credit if the warranty is never used.
An extended warranty can typically still be purchased later, even after the original sale, as long as it's bought before the factory warranty expires
A third-party extended warranty is a separate product from a manufacturer's own extended service plan and may have different claims practices.
Extended warranty contracts contain exclusions that are not always explained verbally when the contract is sold.
A warranty company can treat any sign of an unrelated prior issue as grounds to call a claim pre-existing and deny it.

Most extended warranties are technically cancelable for a pro-rated refund, but the multi-step process (forms, notarization, odometer statements, 60-90 day processing) discourages many buyers from finishing it
A repair shop typically is not paid by the warranty company for the diagnostic time needed to determine the cause of a failure.
Having an aftermarket warranty does not guarantee that a claim will be approved; a substantial share of claims get denied.
When a warranty company approves a claim, it may pay the shop less than its normal labor and parts rate, and the shop may pass the difference to the customer.
GAP coverage may not cover the full gap between a total-loss payout and the remaining loan balance in every case.
A dealer is not automatically liable for ambiguous wording in an add-on contract as long as claims are honored under state law.
A lawsuit claiming an add-on coverage product is a scam can fail in court when the plaintiff never filed a claim and suffered no loss.
The vehicle value used to determine a GAP payout is set by whichever is higher: the insurer's valuation or the vehicle's book value.
A telemarketing operation can pose as being affiliated with vehicle manufacturers to sell 'extended warranties' deceptively.
A seller of extended vehicle warranties can falsely claim its product offers 'bumper to bumper' protection when it does not.
Regulators can permanently ban operators from the extended auto warranty industry and from telemarketing after a scam is proven.
A telemarketing extended-warranty scam can target hundreds of thousands of consumers nationwide.
A government agency can distribute refund checks to consumers years after they were harmed by a deceptive extended-warranty telemarketing scheme.
A large-scale telemarketing extended-warranty scam can result in tens of thousands of consumers receiving refunds from a single settlement.
FTC refund checks must be cashed within a set window or the refund may be forfeited.
Salespeople can earn commissions of up to half the price of an extended warranty
The company that sells the extended warranty decides what repairs are covered, not an independent party
Extended warranty contracts are often written with a mix of legal and technical jargon that makes them hard for an average buyer to fully understand
A warranty provider can go out of business, leaving a purchased extended warranty contract worthless
Luxury and European brand cars break down more as they age, making extended warranty payouts likely to exceed what was paid for the policy
Claim approval rates vary widely between extended warranty companies, and some approve less than half of the repairs that shops believe should be covered
Extended warranty companies that spend the most on marketing tend to be lower-rated for coverage and service
Choosing a vehicle model with a better-than-average reliability rating and maintaining it properly reduces the likelihood of needing extended warranty coverage
Manufacturer warranties on major appliances typically last only about one year for parts and labor
Extended warranty policies often cover accidental damage, which a standard manufacturer's warranty never covers
Extended warranty claims can be capped by a maximum number of claims or a monetary limit, after which the policy becomes void
Extended warranty policies may include a waiting period before coverage begins, during which damage isn't covered
Some extended warranties offer new-for-old replacement of the product when a repair isn't feasible, rather than just a repair

Dealership service advisors often work on commission, creating a financial incentive to recommend unnecessary service
Dealership service departments generate more profit for a dealership than new and used car sales
Dealerships don't always proactively tell customers about safety recalls on their vehicle during a service visit
Skipping maintenance tasks recommended by a dealership service advisor that go beyond the manufacturer's owner's manual schedule does not void a vehicle's factory warranty
No lender requires a borrower to buy an extended warranty, vehicle service contract, prepaid maintenance, or gap insurance as a condition of approving financing

Canceling a financed add-on product like an extended warranty within a certain window, such as 60 or 90 days, triggers a 'chargeback' that claws back the commission the finance manager earned on the sale
Consumers have a legal right to cancel an extended warranty according to the contract's terms, and a dealership that refuses to honor that can be sued
Extended warranties are more likely to be worth the cost for vehicles driven heavily, since more wear and tear raises the chance of needing a covered repair
Extended warranty list prices carry large profit margins, leaving room to negotiate a lower price
Prepaid dealership maintenance plans often don't cover the most expensive maintenance items, like tires, brakes, and fluid changes, reducing their value compared to paying out of pocket
Dealerships often pressure customers to decide on a service contract or extended warranty purchase immediately, during financing, without time to consider
A warranty provider's own inspector can determine the cause of damage and that finding alone can be used to deny a claim without independent verification.
An extended warranty company can refuse to put the reasons for a claim denial in writing, giving explanations only verbally.
When a warranty company denies a claim, it may offer to refund the customer's premiums instead of paying for the covered repair.
A settlement offer from a warranty company can require the customer to permanently waive any future claims and retract complaints filed with regulators or review sites.
A warranty company's settlement offer can include a non-disparagement clause barring the customer from publicly criticizing the company afterward.
Not every repair shop accepts a given extended warranty provider, which can limit where a customer is able to get a covered repair done.
Extended warranty plans can require extra mandatory surcharges for certain vehicle features, such as four-wheel drive or a turbocharger.
A warranty comparison marketplace can show real, purchasable plan quotes from multiple providers without requiring your phone number or contact info upfront.
Extended warranty plans typically come in tiers, from a basic plan covering core systems to a comprehensive top-tier plan covering nearly everything.
All extended warranty contracts include a short money-back guarantee window for canceling shortly after purchase.
Sites advertising free instant extended-warranty quotes often just collect your contact information and sell it to sales reps who then call repeatedly.
If an extended-warranty seller pressures you with limited-time pricing, it's a tactic to stop you from comparing options rather than an actual price increase.
A legitimate extended warranty provider will give you the full written contract details upfront rather than only quoting a price over the phone.
Extended warranty sellers generate large profits on these contracts while the coverage itself is often limited in what it actually pays for.
Paying for a pre-purchase mechanic inspection and self-insuring by saving the warranty's cost is often cheaper than buying an extended warranty.
When an extended warranty company files for bankruptcy, customers who paid premiums typically recover only a small fraction of what they were owed.

Having an extended warranty makes a customer more likely to return to the selling dealership's service department, creating ongoing revenue beyond the warranty sale.
Keeping organized maintenance and repair records improves the odds that an extended warranty claim gets approved rather than denied.
A warranty company can deny a claim by disputing exactly which part or location caused a covered failure, even when the failure itself isn't in question.
Every financial product sold in a dealership's finance office, including extended warranties, has a negative expected value: on average the buyer gets back less money than they paid in.
The dealership that sells an extended warranty earns a commission on the sale and is a separate company from the one that decides and pays claims.
Canceling a financed extended warranty reduces the loan principal by the refunded amount, while the monthly payment itself stays the same

A major extended-warranty marketer has faced a federal settlement over deceptive advertising about what its plans actually cover.
Checking a warranty company's reputation and reviews before buying can help you avoid an unreliable provider.
A longer multi-year extended warranty term is worth more than a short one.

Extended warranty scam calls are likely timed using public vehicle registration data matched against when a car's factory warranty is due to expire.

Electronics protection plans typically only cover hardware failures, not issues like viruses or ransomware that cause most problems.

Extended warranty solicitation letters use urgent language like 'important' and 'confidential' to make the offer seem official or mandatory

Products commonly fail soon after their manufacturer warranty period ends
An extended warranty gives peace of mind even if it is never used

When a covered product can't be repaired cost-effectively, the warranty provider will replace it with newer technology
Extended warranties and service agreements are essentially a form of insurance

Keeping an extended warranty's deductible at $50 or $100 avoids paying more out of pocket than the deductible on most repairs
